categories.label: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

objectives.text: Differentiate tasks that require nursing judgment from tasks that may be delegated.
Select an appropriate delegatee using patient stability, task predictability, and local scope.
Provide direction, supervision, and outcome evaluation after delegation.

coreLesson.summary: Match the task to the delegatee, retain nursing judgment, communicate expectations, and evaluate the result.

sections.heading: Decision frame
sections.body: The nurse assesses the patient and task before delegating. Assessment, teaching, evaluation, and unstable-patient decisions remain with the licensed nurse.

sections.heading: Communication
sections.body: State the task, expected result, reporting parameters, and time frame. Confirm understanding and availability for questions.

sections.heading: Supervision
sections.body: Delegation transfers performance of a task, not accountability for the nursing decision. Reassess the patient and evaluate completion.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A newly admitted patient has changing neurologic findings. Which action is the priority?

options.text: The registered nurse performs the focused assessment and determines the next intervention.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: An unstable or changing condition requires licensed nursing assessment and judgment.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A stable patient needs routine intake and output recorded. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Delegate measurement with clear reporting parameters and review the result.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: A predictable task may be delegated when direction and supervision are provided.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A patient requires initial teaching for a new diagnosis. Which action is the priority?

options.text: The registered nurse performs and evaluates the initial teaching.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Initial teaching and evaluation require nursing judgment.

options.text: Assess the patient and determine the appropriate nursing response.

Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: The nurse must interpret abnormal findings and act on the patient response.

objectives.text: Apply standard precautions to every patient encounter.
Select PPE from the anticipated exposure.
Respond safely to a sharps or body-fluid exposure.

coreLesson.summary: Select hand hygiene and protective equipment from the anticipated exposure, then remove equipment without contaminating clean areas.

sections.heading: Anticipate exposure
sections.body: Standard precautions apply to every patient. Add gloves, gown, mask, and eye protection according to likely contact with blood, body fluids, mucous membranes, nonintact skin, or contaminated equipment.

sections.heading: Hand hygiene
sections.body: Perform hand hygiene at indicated moments and after glove removal. Gloves do not replace hand hygiene.

sections.heading: Exposure response
sections.body: Immediately wash or flush the exposed area, report the event, and follow the organization's exposure evaluation process.

focusedReview: Standard precautions apply to all patients.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A procedure may splash body fluid toward the face. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Use gloves plus facial and eye protection appropriate to the splash risk.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: PPE selection is based on the anticipated route and extent of exposure.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: Gloves are removed after contact with contaminated material. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Perform hand hygiene immediately after glove removal.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Gloves can have defects and hands can be contaminated during removal.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A nurse sustains a needlestick injury. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Wash the area, report promptly, and begin the exposure protocol.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Immediate cleansing and timely evaluation reduce preventable harm and enable indicated prophylaxis.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: Clean supplies are placed near used wound-care materials. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Separate clean and contaminated fields before continuing care.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Maintaining separation limits indirect transmission.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A nurse plans to recap a used needle by hand. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Activate the safety device and place the needle directly in an approved sharps container.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Avoiding manipulation of used sharps reduces percutaneous injury risk.

topic.title: Postpartum Discharge Teaching and Warning Signs

objectives.text: Distinguish expected postpartum changes from warning signs.
Prioritize urgent follow-up instructions.
Use teach-back to verify understanding.

coreLesson.summary: Teach expected recovery, self-care, follow-up, and urgent warning signs using confirmation of understanding.

sections.heading: Expected recovery
sections.body: Explain the usual progression of lochia, comfort measures, hydration, rest, and follow-up while emphasizing that symptoms must be interpreted with the whole clinical picture.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.body: Urgent evaluation is needed for heavy bleeding, breathing difficulty, chest pain, seizure, severe headache with concerning features, or thoughts of self-harm or harming the infant.

sections.heading: Teach-back
sections.body: Ask the patient to explain when and how they would obtain help; correct gaps and include the support person when desired.

focusedReview: Heavy bleeding and cardiopulmonary symptoms require urgent action.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient reports soaking a pad rapidly with ongoing heavy bleeding. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Direct the patient to obtain urgent evaluation for possible postpartum hemorrhage.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Heavy postpartum bleeding can represent a time-sensitive maternal emergency.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient reports sudden shortness of breath and chest pain. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Instruct the patient to activate emergency services immediately.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Acute cardiopulmonary symptoms may indicate a life-threatening complication.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient expresses thoughts of harming themself or the infant. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Maintain safety and arrange immediate emergency mental-health evaluation.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Thoughts of harm require immediate safety intervention, not routine follow-up.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient cannot state whom to contact for worsening symptoms. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Repeat the escalation plan and use teach-back before discharge.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Teach-back identifies and corrects gaps in actionable discharge knowledge.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient reports unilateral leg swelling and pain. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Arrange prompt evaluation for a possible thromboembolic complication.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Unilateral pain and swelling can signal venous thrombosis and require timely assessment.

objectives.text: Select therapeutic responses to distress.
Avoid common nontherapeutic communication barriers.
Escalate statements that indicate possible self-harm.

coreLesson.summary: Use presence, observation, open invitations, reflection, and direct safety assessment without false reassurance or judgment.

sections.heading: Create space
sections.body: Use calm presence, observations, and open invitations that allow the patient to set the pace and describe their experience.

sections.heading: Clarify
sections.body: Reflect or restate the patient's meaning and ask focused questions when safety or symptoms require clarification.

sections.heading: Assess safety
sections.body: Statements suggesting hopelessness or self-harm require direct, nonjudgmental assessment and immediate protection according to risk.

focusedReview: Ask directly about self-harm when indicated.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A patient says, “Nothing will ever get better.” Which action is the priority?

options.text: Acknowledge the distress and ask directly about thoughts of self-harm.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Hopeless statements warrant therapeutic exploration and direct safety assessment.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A grieving patient becomes silent and tearful. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Remain present and allow silence while offering the patient time to speak.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Therapeutic silence communicates presence without forcing conversation.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A patient says, “Everyone is judging me.” Which action is the priority?

options.text: Respond, “It sounds as though you feel judged; tell me more about that.”
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Reflection validates the expressed feeling and invites clarification.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A patient is anxious about a procedure. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Ask what concerns them most and provide information responsive to that concern.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Open exploration identifies the patient's need before teaching.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The nurse is tempted to say, “Everything will be fine.” Which action is the priority?

options.text: Acknowledge uncertainty and explore the patient's specific concern instead.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: False reassurance can close communication and minimize distress.

objectives.text: Identify modifiable pressure-injury risks.
Select individualized prevention interventions.
Evaluate skin response and update the plan.

coreLesson.summary: Identify individual pressure-injury risks and combine repositioning, surface selection, moisture management, nutrition, and skin reassessment.

sections.heading: Risk assessment
sections.body: Assess mobility, sensation, moisture, perfusion, nutrition, friction, shear, devices, and current skin findings.

sections.heading: Prevention bundle
sections.body: Use individualized repositioning, pressure redistribution, heel off-loading, moisture protection, nutrition support, and device checks.

sections.heading: Evaluate
sections.body: Inspect high-risk areas and device contact points, document changes, and revise the prevention plan when skin tolerance worsens.

focusedReview: Escalate new nonblanching or worsening skin changes.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: An immobile patient slides down repeatedly in bed. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Reposition with lift assistance and reduce shear while supporting alignment.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Dragging and sliding increase shear forces that damage tissue.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: Moisture is trapped against the sacral skin. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Cleanse gently, manage the moisture source, and apply an appropriate moisture barrier.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Persistent moisture weakens the skin barrier and increases injury risk.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A medical device rests tightly against the patient's skin. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Inspect beneath and around the device and relieve avoidable pressure.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Medical devices can concentrate pressure and conceal evolving injury.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient has limited mobility and poor nutritional intake. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Initiate a coordinated prevention plan including mobility and nutrition interventions.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Multiple risks require a bundled, interdisciplinary approach.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A high-risk area shows a new persistent color change. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Relieve pressure, reassess the area, document the finding, and escalate per policy.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Early recognition and pressure relief help prevent progression.

objectives.text: Identify safeguards for high-alert medications.
Recognize parameters that require holding and clarification.
Monitor for therapeutic and adverse effects.

coreLesson.summary: Verify the complete medication order, patient-specific parameters, independent checks when required, monitoring, and response to harm.

sections.heading: Before administration
sections.body: Verify patient identity, medication, indication, dose, route, time, allergies, relevant laboratory data, interactions, and required independent checks.

sections.heading: During administration
sections.body: Use the correct equipment and rate, minimize interruptions, and do not bypass smart-device or barcode safeguards without resolving the cause.

sections.heading: After administration
sections.body: Monitor the expected effect and predictable harms, document the response, and act immediately on evidence of an adverse event.

focusedReview: Know why the patient is receiving the medication.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The prescribed dose is inconsistent with the available concentration and usual range. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Hold administration and clarify the order before preparing the dose.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: A dose discrepancy must be resolved before medication reaches the patient.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A required patient-specific laboratory result is unavailable. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Obtain or verify the required result before administering the medication.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Relevant laboratory data can determine whether administration is safe.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: Barcode scanning produces a mismatch alert. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Stop and resolve the patient, medication, and order mismatch.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: A mismatch alert is a safety signal and should not be bypassed for convenience.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: Policy requires an independent double check for this medication. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Have the qualified second clinician independently verify the required elements.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: An independent check is performed separately to reduce shared-error bias.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient develops signs of an acute adverse reaction during administration. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Stop the medication when appropriate, assess the patient, and activate the emergency response pathway.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Immediate assessment and response limit ongoing exposure and address instability.

topic.title: Recognition of an Acute Transfusion Reaction

objectives.text: Recognize findings associated with a possible transfusion reaction.
Sequence immediate nursing actions.
Complete required notification and specimen/product handling.

coreLesson.summary: Recognize new symptoms during transfusion, stop the blood product, maintain access with appropriate compatible fluid and tubing per policy, assess, and notify.

sections.heading: Recognize
sections.body: Treat new fever, chills, dyspnea, chest or back discomfort, hypotension, urticaria, or other acute change during transfusion as a possible reaction until evaluated.

sections.heading: Stop and assess
sections.body: Stop the transfusion immediately, maintain venous access using new tubing and compatible solution according to policy, assess the patient, and obtain vital signs.

sections.heading: Notify and investigate
sections.body: Notify the provider and transfusion service, follow emergency orders, and send the product, tubing, or specimens as required by organizational policy.

focusedReview: Assess airway, breathing, circulation, and vital signs.
Do not restart the implicated unit.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient develops chills and dyspnea shortly after a transfusion begins. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Stop the transfusion immediately and assess the patient.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Stopping exposure and assessing stability are the immediate priorities for a suspected reaction.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The transfusion has been stopped for a suspected reaction. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Maintain venous access with new tubing and compatible solution according to policy.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Separate tubing avoids infusing residual blood while preserving access for treatment.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient's blood pressure is falling during the reaction. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Activate urgent assistance and support airway, breathing, and circulation while following emergency orders.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Hemodynamic instability requires immediate escalation and resuscitative priorities.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: Symptoms improve after the unit is stopped. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Continue the reaction protocol and do not restart the implicated blood product.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Improvement does not establish that the product is safe to resume.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A possible reaction has been stabilized. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Notify the provider and transfusion service and complete required specimens and documentation.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Investigation and reporting support diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of further harm.

topic.title: Early Recognition and Escalation of Sepsis

objectives.text: Recognize clinical deterioration consistent with possible sepsis.
Prioritize immediate assessment and escalation.
Evaluate response to time-sensitive interventions.

coreLesson.summary: Recognize a concerning infection-associated change, assess perfusion and organ function, and activate the local sepsis pathway without delaying stabilization.

sections.heading: Recognize change
sections.body: Possible infection plus altered mentation, abnormal perfusion, respiratory change, hypotension, reduced urine output, or other new organ dysfunction requires urgent assessment.

sections.heading: Escalate
sections.body: Activate the organization's sepsis or rapid-response pathway, communicate the trend and suspected source, obtain ordered diagnostics promptly, and begin stabilization.

sections.heading: Evaluate
sections.body: Trend mental status, perfusion, blood pressure, oxygenation, urine output, laboratory results, and response to treatment; escalate persistent deterioration.

focusedReview: Trend changes rather than relying on one value.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: A patient with suspected infection develops new confusion and hypotension. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Activate urgent sepsis evaluation and assess airway, breathing, circulation, and perfusion.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Possible infection with new organ dysfunction and hypotension requires immediate escalation.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: Urine output is falling while heart rate and respiratory rate rise. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Report the deterioration promptly and reassess perfusion and the full vital-sign trend.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: The combined trend can signal worsening organ perfusion.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: The patient has a possible infection but a normal temperature. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Continue evaluating for sepsis using the complete clinical picture and organ-function findings.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: A normal temperature does not exclude serious infection or sepsis.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: Ordered cultures and treatment are pending while the patient deteriorates. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Coordinate time-sensitive diagnostics and treatment while continuing stabilization and escalation.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Deterioration requires parallel action rather than waiting passively for one step to finish.

assessmentItems.stem: During the initial assessment, the nurse notes: Blood pressure remains low after initial interventions. Which action is the priority?

options.text: Escalate immediately and continue reassessing perfusion and treatment response.
Delay action until the end of the shift.
Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.

assessmentItems.rationale: Persistent hypotension indicates ongoing instability and need for higher-level support.
